Those lists blow past the 30字 chip limit, repeat what all sides share, and add the model's own judgment words. The diff mostly repeats facts already shown in the side lines, and clean() lets 50字 zh lines through and can show English lines cut off mid-word.","findings":[{"severity":"high","what":"The diff repeats what the side lines above it already say. This breaks 'insight, not repetition'. sidesRecap does not catch partial overlap.","evidence":"Ex1 diff: 「只看右派會漏掉平民死亡人數與彈劾程序解說；…則不知民主黨表態支持並預告一月還有行動」. The c line already says 「著墨『三百多名』平民死者與彈劾程序說明」 and the r line says 「也提到民主黨有後續動作」. Ex0 diff 「只有中間標題提到伊朗」 repeats the c line 「並稱伊朗戰爭正確」.","fix":"Define diff as a fact that no side line mentions, naming which side has it. Give an example of what does not count. Return \"\" when every gap is already covered."},{"severity":"high","what":"Side lines ignore the 30字 limit and list every headline instead of one angle. This makes unreadable chips, and clean() lets lines up to 50字 through.","evidence":"Ex1 r zh: 「引述赫格塞斯與萬斯駁斥，稱彈劾是「政治奇觀」「鬧劇」，並連結到攻擊川普與軍人；也提到民主黨有後續動作。」 is about 50字. Ex1 c and l zh are about 45字 each. clean(): `if (String(x?.zh || '').trim().length > 50) continue;`.","fix":"Ask for one framing point per side as a hard 30字 limit. Tighten clean() to about 34 characters, allowing small slack."},{"severity":"medium","what":"Side lines include facts every side shares, which the prompt forbids. The side-line instruction ('stress or leave out') also overlaps the diff, which causes the duplication.","evidence":"Ex1 l zh: 「也報導赫格塞斯的反擊」. All three sides carry Hegseth's counterattack, e.g. r 'Hegseth ties impeachment efforts…', c 'It's a farce'. Ex0 b zh: 「未交代原因與提案者」 is a leave-out fact that belongs in diff.","fix":"Side line = framing only: what it leads with, who it quotes, its word choice. Missing facts go to diff. Give an explicit example of a shared fact to skip."},{"severity":"medium","what":"The model adds its own judging words about an outlet's headline, which breaks the neutrality rule.","evidence":"Ex1 c zh: 「另有嘲諷赫格塞斯言論的標題」 and en 'plus a mocking take on his remarks'. The headline itself ('Low-T Tirade… Dissected') never says mocking.","fix":"Ban evaluative words unless they translate a headline's own word, and list examples (嘲諷/mocking, 聳動)."},{"severity":"medium","what":"Numbers are spelled out in Chinese, so they likely slip past numbersFrom and the headline's figure is not reproduced exactly.","evidence":"Ex1 c zh: 「三百多名」 for the headline's 'Over 300'.","fix":"Require numbers in digits exactly as the headline writes them (300, not 三百)."},{"severity":"medium","what":"clean() truncates English lines at 160/200 characters mid-word instead of dropping them. Its own comment says over-long lines are left out, but only zh is checked. The diff zh threshold of 70 is far above the 40字 limit.","evidence":"`const zh = str(x?.zh, 50), en = str(x?.en, 160);` with no en length check. `const whole = String(it.diff?.zh || '').trim().length <= 70;` lets Ex1's roughly 48字 diff through.","fix":"Skip a side whose raw en exceeds 160 characters. Require diff zh of 46 or less and diff en of 200 or less before showing it."},{"severity":"low","what":"Names across languages are undefined. 'Names as the headlines write them' cannot apply when en is written from Chinese headlines, or zh from English ones, so the model invents romanizations or transliterations.","evidence":"Ex0 en: 'Liao Yu-hui', 'Chang Shan-cheng', 'Chiang', 'Shen' are all model-made from 廖玉蕙/張善政/蔣萬安/沈伯洋. Ex1 zh must transliterate Vance and Hegseth.","fix":"Use Taiwan media's usual Chinese form for well-known foreign names and otherwise keep the English. Use the person's known romanization, or a role the headlines give, rather than guessing."},{"severity":"low","what":"Runs only on top-tier models with a 90s timeout, against the 'cheap models for most' rule.","evidence":"`models: ['sonnet', 'sol'], timeoutMs: 90_000`","fix":"After tightening the prompt, test on Haiku 5.5 / GPT Luna with the examples below. Keep Sonnet only if cheap models fail the neutrality or diff checks."}],"edits":[{"old":"For each story, for each side it gives (and only those): what that side’s headlines stress or leave out: their angle, who they quote, the words they choose. Not the facts every side shares. zh: at most 30 字, Traditional Chinese (台灣用語) with full-width punctuation (，：；); en: at most 18 words.","new":"For each story, for each side it gives (and only those): the one framing choice that sets that side’s headlines apart from the other sides: what they lead with, who they quote, or the word they choose. One point, not a list of its headlines. Never mention anything every side’s headlines say (if all sides report his reply, leave it out). Facts a side leaves out go in diff, not here. zh: at most 30 字 counting punctuation (hard limit: longer lines are thrown away), Traditional Chinese (台灣用語) with full-width punctuation (，：；); en: at most 18 words, the same point as zh.","why":"Stops list-style 45–50字 lines, shared facts, and overlap with diff."},{"old":"diff: what a reader of only one side would miss: a fact, a voice or a number one side reports and another leaves out (zh at most 40 字, en at most 24 words). The reader already sees each side’s line above it: never restate or sum them up, never quote a word they quote; both \"\" when nothing is left out.","new":"diff: one fact, voice or number that a reader of one side would miss AND that none of your side lines already mentions; say which side has it and which lacks it (e.g. 只有偏綠標題提到…). zh at most 40 字, en at most 24 words, one point, zh and en saying the same thing. The reader already sees each side’s line above it: if a side line already names it (e.g. that line mentions Iran), it does not count. Never restate or sum up the lines, never quote a word they quote. Both \"\" when no such fact is left.","why":"Both examples' diffs repeated the side lines; this makes the no-repeat test concrete for cheaper models."},{"old":"Never say which side is right, never call an outlet biased or propaganda, add no adjective of your own about anyone. Every number you write must be in the headlines. Names as the headlines write them.","new":"Never say which side is right, never call an outlet biased or propaganda, and add no word of your own that judges a headline or a person (not 嘲諷/mocking, 聳動/sensational, 強硬/hardline) unless it translates that headline’s own word. Every number you write must be in the headlines, written in digits as the headline writes it (300, not 三百; 1原因 stays 1). Names as the headlines write them. In zh, a foreign name in the Chinese form Taiwan media use (Hegseth = 赫格塞斯, Vance = 萬斯); if you don’t know it, keep the English name. In en, a Taiwanese name in that person’s known romanization (蔣萬安 = Chiang Wan-an); if unsure, use a role the headlines give (the mayor) instead of guessing.","why":"Fixes 「嘲諷」/'mocking', 「三百多名」, and invented romanizations or transliterations."},{"old":"if (String(x?.zh || '').trim().length > 50) continue;","new":"if (String(x?.zh || '').trim().length > 34 || String(x?.en || '').trim().length > 160) continue;","why":"The 50 threshold let 45–50字 lines into 30字 chips. en was silently cut mid-word at 160."},{"old":"const whole = String(it.diff?.zh || '').trim().length <= 70;","new":"const whole = String(it.diff?.zh || '').trim().length <= 46 && String(it.diff?.en || '').trim().length <= 200;","why":"Matches the 40字 limit with small slack and stops en diffs being cut mid-word at 200."}],"examples":[{"name":"shared fact must not appear in lines","input":"[{\"id\":\"t1\",\"region\":\"tw\",\"sides\":{\"g\":[\"台電宣布明年電價凍漲 經濟部：照顧民生\",\"電價凍漲 經濟部長：產業用電也不調\"],\"c\":[\"明年電價凍漲 台電累積虧損逾4000億\",\"電價審議會決議凍漲 台電虧損待補\"],\"b\":[\"電價凍漲 台電虧損4000億誰買單？\",\"凍漲背後 藍委批政府拿預算填台電\"]}}]","expect":"No side line mentions 凍漲 itself, since every side has it. The lines are about framing: g quotes 經濟部 and 照顧民生; b quotes 藍委 and 誰買單. The diff says only c and b give the 4000億 loss, written as 4000, and that fact is not already in a side line. No judging words. Each zh 30字 or less."},{"name":"near-identical headlines give empty diff","input":"[{\"id\":\"t2\",\"region\":\"tw\",\"sides\":{\"g\":[\"颱風山陀兒明晨登陸 南部停班停課\"],\"c\":[\"山陀兒颱風明晨登陸 南部縣市停班停課\"],\"b\":[\"山陀兒明晨登陸南台灣 多縣市停班停課\"]}}]","expect":"Diff is both \"\". Side lines are short, give no invented differences in angle, and add no facts. Being dropped by clean() is acceptable if no side has a real angle."},{"name":"evaluative headline must not be judged","input":"[{\"id\":\"w1\",\"region\":\"intl\",\"sides\":{\"l\":[\"Trump's Tariff Meltdown: Dissected\",\"Economists warn new tariffs could cost families $2,000 a year\"],\"c\":[\"US raises tariffs on Chinese EVs to 100%\",\"Explainer: What the new tariffs cover\"],\"r\":[\"Trump hits China with 100% EV tariff, vows to protect autoworkers\"]}}]","expect":"No 嘲諷/mocking/sarcastic unless translating a headline word. Numbers appear as digits exactly as the headlines give them: 100%, $2,000, never 兩千. The l line can quote 「崩潰」 as a translation of 'Meltdown'. The diff names that only l gives the $2,000 family cost, if no line already said it."},{"name":"lesser-known foreign name","input":"[{\"id\":\"w2\",\"region\":\"intl\",\"sides\":{\"l\":[\"Rep. Jasmine Crockett grills FBI director over agent firings\"],\"c\":[\"FBI director Kash Patel faces House questions on dismissals\",\"Patel defends firing of 20 agents\"],\"r\":[\"Patel fires back at Crockett: 'Political theater'\"]}}]","expect":"zh uses 帕特爾 for Patel only if confident, otherwise keeps 'Patel'/'Crockett' in English; it never invents a transliteration. 20 stays 20. The diff notes that only c gives the number 20 fired. No line describes anyone as aggressive."},{"name":"only one side covered plus a two-side story","input":"[{\"id\":\"t3\",\"region\":\"tw\",\"sides\":{\"b\":[\"立委爆國防部採購案疑點 要求說明\"]}},{\"id\":\"t4\",\"region\":\"tw\",\"sides\":{\"g\":[\"賴清德出訪友邦 簽署3項合作協議\"],\"b\":[\"賴清德出訪 過境美國細節未公布\"]}}]","expect":"t3 gives no invented c or g lines; skipping it or giving only a b line is fine, and clean() drops it. t4 has only g and b lines, with no c. The diff says only g mentions the 3 agreements and only b mentions the undisclosed US transit, without repeating the side lines."},{"name":"many headlines stress the 30字 limit","input":"[{\"id\":\"t5\",\"region\":\"tw\",\"sides\":{\"g\":[\"罷免案通過 民進黨：民意展現\",\"罷免成功 公民團體街頭慶祝\",\"罷免投票率3成5 創新高\",\"選委會：開票過程順利\"],\"c\":[\"罷免案過關 投票率35%\",\"罷免通過 下一步補選時程出爐\",\"國民黨：尊重結果但遺憾\",\"罷免後立院席次變化一次看\"],\"b\":[\"罷免通過 國民黨團：民主倒退\",\"罷免案藍委下台 支持者淚灑現場\",\"罷免投票率僅3成5 多數未投\",\"藍營：將提行政訴訟\"]}}]","expect":"Each side zh is 30字 or less and makes one framing point: g 民意展現 or 創新高 versus b 僅 or 多數未投, both on the same turnout figure. It does not list all four headlines. 3成5 and 35% are kept as written. The diff names one fact absent from all lines, such as b's planned 行政訴訟 or c's 補選 timing, or is \"\"."}]}

{"verdict":"The example cards are mostly usable: sentences are natural, short and in Taiwan Chinese, and clean() drops cards that do not use the word. The weak parts are the confuse chips, the hooks and the spelling rule. Confuse chips list word-family members with no meaning attached, hooks drift into Latin or repeat the meaning, and the loose \"plain form\" rule lets irregular forms and phrases get silently thrown away by clean().","findings":[{"severity":"high","what":"confuse lists word-family members rather than real mix-ups, and gives each as a bare English word. A chip saying only \"option\" tells the learner nothing they cannot see; they still cannot tell the two words apart.","evidence":"able → \"confuse\":[\"enable\",\"disable\"]; review → [\"preview\",\"interview\"]; opt → [\"adopt\",\"option\"]. Prompt: \"up to 3 English words learners mix it up with (look or sound alike, or near meanings)\".","fix":"Ask only for words students actually misuse for this one, such as look- or sound-alikes (abandon/abundant) or near-synonyms used differently. Exclude words built from it or sharing its root. Write each as \"word 中文意思\" so the chip itself shows the difference. Adjust clean()'s self-filter for the new format."},{"severity":"medium","what":"The rule for using the word is vague (\"a plain form of it\"). clean() only keeps sentences that contain the first 3–5 letters of the word. Irregular forms (teach→taught, go→went, mouse→mice) and 3-letter drop-e forms (use→using) are silently dropped, and a card with both sentences dropped disappears.","evidence":"Prompt: \"Use the word itself or a plain form of it.\" clean(): `.filter(e => ... e.en.toLowerCase().includes(stem))`, then `if (!ex.length) continue;`. For \"teach\" the stem is \"tea\", so \"She taught us\" fails.","fix":"Tell the model the exact rule: the word as given or with a regular -s/-ed/-ing ending, never an irregular form. Say that other sentences are thrown out."},{"severity":"medium","what":"Multi-word entries (phrasal verbs) break clean()'s stem check. The stem is cut from the whole phrase and includes a space, so any inflected first word fails.","evidence":"For \"look forward to\" the stem is `w.toLowerCase().slice(0, 5)` = \"look \". \"I'm looking forward to it\" does not contain \"look \", so the card is dropped.","fix":"Compute the stem from the first word of the entry only."},{"severity":"medium","what":"The Chinese translation is bent to fit the given gloss even when the English sentence does not carry that sense. This produces an unnatural or wrong translation.","evidence":"\"The manager asked us to review the proposal carefully.\" → \"經理要我們仔細檢討這份提案。\" Reviewing a proposal is 審閱／審查; 檢討 means reflecting on faults.","fix":"Have the model write a sentence that truly uses the given meaning, rather than forcing the translation. When two meanings are listed, give one sentence for each."},{"severity":"medium","what":"Hooks break the plain-words rule or simply repeat the meaning the card already shows. Meanwhile a genuinely hard word gets no hook.","evidence":"reluctant: \"源自拉丁文 reluctari「抗拒」，luct 有掙扎、抗拒之意\" (a Latin word a student can't use). ambiguous: \"如 ambidextrous 雙手都靈活\" (rare word). opt: \"…選了就是做選擇\" (restates 選擇). abandon: \"\" although it is not an easy word.","fix":"Require parts visible in the spelling, explained with words a high-school student knows. Ban Latin/Greek source words and rare example words, and ban ending on the meaning. Say that \"\" is for words a student already knows, and that harder words usually deserve a hook."},{"severity":"low","what":"There is no bound on batch size, so cost and latency are open-ended. clean() accepts up to 200 cards, and each card is roughly 150 output tokens. A large word list risks hitting the 60 s timeout or the model's output cap, and a truncated answer is lost as a whole batch.","evidence":"`list(raw?.cards, 200)`, `timeoutMs: 60_000`. The prompt doesn't limit the number of words.","fix":"The caller should chunk the list to about 15–20 words per request; this lives in caller code, outside this source."}],"edits":[{"old":"'ex: two short, natural example sentences (≤ 14 words each) using the word in that meaning, each with a natural Traditional Chinese translation (台灣用語). Use the word itself or a plain form of it.',","new":"'ex: two short, natural example sentences (≤ 14 words each) from school or daily life, using the word in the meaning given (if two meanings are listed, one sentence for each). Each English sentence must contain the word exactly as given, or with only a regular ending added (-s, -es, -ed, -ing); never an irregular form (teach → taught, go → went, mouse → mice): such sentences are thrown out. zh: a natural translation in Traditional Chinese as Taiwan says it (台灣用語，全形標點). If the natural Chinese would not be the given meaning, write a different English sentence instead of forcing the translation.',","why":"Matches clean()'s stem check so cards are not silently dropped, and stops translations bent to fit the gloss (檢討這份提案)."},{"old":"'hook: one memory hook in Traditional Chinese, ≤ 30 字: a real word root or word parts (e.g. “re- 再 + view 看”), a sound-alike, or a vivid picture tying the spelling to the meaning. Never just restate the meaning or the example; no made-up roots. \"\" when there is no hook that truly helps (most easy words).',","new":"'hook: one memory hook in Traditional Chinese, ≤ 30 字: word parts you can see in the spelling (e.g. “re- 再 + view 看”), a sound-alike, or a vivid picture tying the spelling to the meaning. Explain parts with words a high-school student already knows: no Latin or Greek source words (not “reluctari”), no rare example words (not “ambidextrous”), only roots you are sure are real. Do not end by repeating the meaning; the card already shows it. \"\" only for words a student already knows (like able, happy); harder words usually deserve a hook.',","why":"Stops Latin and rare-word hooks and meaning restatements, and stops hard words like abandon getting no hook."},{"old":"'confuse: up to 3 English words learners mix it up with (look or sound alike, or near meanings), [] when none.',","new":"'confuse: up to 3 English words students really misuse for this one: look or sound alike (abandon / abundant, affect / effect) or near meaning used differently. Each written as \"word 中文意思\", e.g. \"abundant 豐富的\". Not words built from it or sharing its root (enable, disable, preview, option are family, not confusions). [] when none.',","why":"Makes the chip show the difference the learner can't see, and removes word-family padding."},{"old":"const stem = w.toLowerCase().slice(0, Math.max(3, Math.min(5, w.length - 2)));","new":"const head = w.toLowerCase().split(/\\s+/)[0];\n        const stem = head.slice(0, Math.max(3, Math.min(5, head.length - 2)));","why":"For phrases like \"look forward to\" the old stem was \"look \" (with the space), which rejected every inflected sentence."},{"old":".filter(x => x && x.toLowerCase() !== w.toLowerCase())","new":".filter(x => x && x.toLowerCase() !== w.toLowerCase() && !x.toLowerCase().startsWith(w.toLowerCase() + ' '))","why":"With confuse items now written as \"word 中文\", the self-match check must also catch the word itself followed by a gloss."}],"examples":[{"name":"irregular and drop-e verbs","input":"{\"words\":[{\"w\":\"teach\",\"zh\":\"v. 教\"},{\"w\":\"buy\",\"zh\":\"v. 買\"},{\"w\":\"go\",\"zh\":\"v. 去\"},{\"w\":\"use\",\"zh\":\"v. 使用\"},{\"w\":\"lie\",\"zh\":\"v. 說謊\"}]}","expect":"Every card survives clean() with 2 sentences. English uses teach/teaches/teaching, buy/buys, go/goes, use/uses/used, lie/lies/lied. There must be no taught, bought, went, using or lying (lying passes clean but should be avoided). lie is used as 說謊, not 躺."},{"name":"phrasal verbs","input":"{\"words\":[{\"w\":\"look forward to\",\"zh\":\"phr. 期待\"},{\"w\":\"give up\",\"zh\":\"phr. 放棄\"},{\"w\":\"take off\",\"zh\":\"phr. （飛機）起飛\"}]}","expect":"Cards are kept, including sentences like \"We are looking forward to the trip.\" take off is used only in the plane sense. confuse may list real mix-ups such as \"put off 延後\", not repeats of the phrase."},{"name":"two senses and two parts of speech","input":"{\"words\":[{\"w\":\"present\",\"zh\":\"v. 呈現；adj. 出席的\"},{\"w\":\"review\",\"zh\":\"v. 複習；檢討\"},{\"w\":\"run\",\"zh\":\"v. 經營\"}]}","expect":"present gets one verb sentence and one adjective sentence (\"All students were present.\" → 出席). Each zh translation is natural and actually means the listed sense; nothing like 檢討這份提案. run is used only as 經營 (run a shop), not 跑."},{"name":"classic confusables","input":"{\"words\":[{\"w\":\"affect\",\"zh\":\"v. 影響\"},{\"w\":\"accept\",\"zh\":\"v. 接受\"},{\"w\":\"desert\",\"zh\":\"n. 沙漠\"},{\"w\":\"quiet\",\"zh\":\"adj. 安靜的\"}]}","expect":"confuse contains glossed items such as \"effect 效果\", \"except 除了\", \"dessert 甜點\", \"quite 相當\". No family words (affection, acceptance), and no bare words without 中文."},{"name":"hard words needing plain hooks","input":"{\"words\":[{\"w\":\"benevolent\",\"zh\":\"adj. 仁慈的\"},{\"w\":\"procrastinate\",\"zh\":\"v. 拖延\"},{\"w\":\"abandon\",\"zh\":\"v. 放棄、拋棄\"},{\"w\":\"vulnerable\",\"zh\":\"adj. 脆弱的、易受傷的\"}]}","expect":"Each gets a non-empty hook ≤ 30 字 built from parts visible in the spelling (bene- 好, pro- 向前 + cras 明天), a sound-alike or a picture. Hooks contain no Latin source words or rare English words, invent no roots, and do not end by restating 仁慈／拖延."},{"name":"easy words and Taiwan wording","input":"{\"words\":[{\"w\":\"happy\",\"zh\":\"adj. 快樂的\"},{\"w\":\"software\",\"zh\":\"n. 軟體\"},{\"w\":\"taxi\",\"zh\":\"n. 計程車\"},{\"w\":\"video\",\"zh\":\"n. 影片\"}]}","expect":"happy has hook \"\". Translations use Taiwan terms (軟體, 計程車, 影片, 捷運, 手機) with 全形標點, never 软件, 出租车, 视频 or 地鐵. confuse is [] rather than padded with related words."}]}

{"verdict":"The feature is mostly sound: most `who` tags are right, non-student posts are emptied, and dates in `line` and `by` are checked against the source. Before it ships, a few things need fixing: an ambiguous rule strips the organizer from headlines, the year logic and the `by` check can put a wrong deadline chip on a post, the grade rules conflict for admissions posts, and `act` can carry numbers nobody checks.","findings":[{"severity":"high","what":"The headline drops the name of an outside school or organizer, so the line no longer says whose event it is.","evidence":"n2 title 「南華大學116學年度特殊選才學系探索線上說明會」 → line 「特殊選才學系探索線上說明會」. The prompt says \"drop 【轉知】, 公告, unit names and the school’s name\", and the cheap model reads that as any school's name. n1 likewise loses 伊甸.","fix":"Say \"this school’s own name\", and explicitly keep an outside school's or organizer's name."},{"severity":"high","what":"The year rules give wrong deadlines, and clean() cannot catch them. \"A month and day alone is the coming one\" turns a date a few days back into next year. 學年度 is never explained, so dates in 115學年度第2學期 can land in 2026. clean() never checks the year. It also accepts any month number and day number found anywhere in the source, not as a pair.","evidence":"Prompt: \"(115年 = 2026; a month and day alone is the coming one)\". clean(): `[String(+by.slice(5, 7)), String(+by.slice(8, 10))].every(n => nums(src).includes(n))`. For n9 (「11/27(五)…17：30離開校園」), by = 2026-11-17 would pass because 17 comes from 17：30. 2027-11-27 would pass too.","fix":"State 民國年 + 1911. Explain that 學年度 is not a year and give each semester's months. Use \"nearest today\" for a bare month and day. In clean(), require month and day adjacent in the source, and the year within ±1 of today's."},{"severity":"medium","what":"The `who` rules conflict for admissions posts, and school divisions are not handled, so tagging is inconsistent.","evidence":"n2 (116學年度特殊選才 talk, which is for current 高三) got [\"some\"] under the outside-talk rule. n3 (四技二專甄選 table) got [\"3\"] under \"升學 = 3\". n3 is also tagged 【進修部】, a separate division, yet day-school 高三 students get it as a grade-3 post.","fix":"Admissions posts (學測, 統測, 特殊選才, 甄選入學, university 說明會) are \"3\" even when the talk is outside.
